The confidence interval widths were calibrated to reflect how uncertainty naturally expands with time. Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals include a sudden and sharp change in interest rate expectations — for example, a surprise Federal Reserve communication or an unexpected inflation print — which could move risk assets sharply in either direction beyond the one-month bounds. It is also worth noting that these intervals were constructed assuming relatively normal market conditions and recent historical volatility as a baseline.
